thread:
maya: quick heads-up — after HF->Redwood conversion of the reranker/embedding pair for the NQ eval, embeddings drifted ~0.68 cosine on our dev set. suspicious it's not quantization only, looks like tokenization/pooling mismatch.

kevin: can you paste the converter command + config.json you used?

maya: sure, ran `redwood-convert --from hf --model sentence-transformers/xxx --target redwood` and the HF config had these partial fields:
```json
{"tokenizer_config": {"add_prefix_space": false, "use_fast": true, "special_tokens_map": {"cls_token": "[CLS]", "sep_token": "[SEP]"}}, "truncation_side": "right"}
```

luis: two quick calls out: 1) HF sometimes maps cls/bos to different token ids (or to `<s>`); converter used a generic mapping and didn't preserve the original `special_tokens_map`. 2) truncation_side differences + pad/truncation semantics (HF's tokenizer may drop CLS or shift offsets) — that will change first-token pooling.

sara: also confirm which pooling the reranker uses. if the reranker eval expects CLS pooling (embedding = hidden_states[0][0]) but our Redwood embedding pipeline was using `mean` or `pooler_output`, you'll see big changes even with identical tokens.

maya: good point — HF model README says "use CLS token (first token)". Redwood converter sets pooler to `first` only if `special_tokens_map` present. I think the missing map caused fallback to `mean`.

kevin: can you repro token ids quickly? small script: 
```python
# compare hf vs converted tokenizer ids
hf_tok = hf_tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=True)
red_tok = redwood_tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=True)
print(hf_tok[:20])
print(red_tok[:20])
```
If those differ at pos 0 (CLS) or positions around truncation boundary we know where the drift comes from.

maya: I ran that. example: "What is the capital of France?"
hf ids: [101, 622, 1110, 1103, 2745, 102]  (CLS=101, SEP=102)
red ids: [1, 622, 1110, 1103, 2745, 2]         (CLS=1, SEP=2)

luis: yep — different special ids. downstream pooling code looked up index 0 expecting CLS embedding, but 1 is the true CLS in HF. so we were pulling a non-CLS token for reranker.

sara: another wrinkle: truncation strategy. Redwood's runtime default was `truncate_longer_sequences=True` with `truncation_side=left` for chat templates; HF model was right-side truncation. on long queries it shifted context and changed tokens included before the CLS.

kevin: quantization note — we ran a 4-bit job and saw an extra ~0.02 drop, but majority (~0.6) came from tokenization/pooling mismatch. so fix tokenization first.

maya: proposed fix: 1) update converter to preserve `special_tokens_map` if present, 2) keep `truncation_side` from HF config (or fail loud), 3) add a `pooling_override` flag in conversion to force `cls|mean|pooler_output`, and 4) add unit tests that compare token id sequences between HF and converted artifact on a small corpus.

luis: strong +1. also add a sanitizer check: if first token id != hf_first_token_id then warn and fail CI for model onboarding.

deploy-bot: scheduled a conversion test job (job id: cj-20260312-78) on dedicated ci-cluster for tomorrow 03:00 UTC to validate changes.

maya: I'll open a PR with converter changes + tests. will also attach a tiny eval harness that compares reranker top-k stability between HF and converted (nq-dev subset).

kevin: if you want help writing the unit test harness I can pair.

maya: thanks — will ping. btw adding this to onboarding checklist: "preserve special_tokens_map, truncation_side, pooling_hint".

sara: nice. once merged let's re-run the NQ eval and the quantized runs and post numbers in #eng-ml. :rocket:

kevin: :thumbsup:

maya: filing follow-ups in the PR description. thanks all.
